question.question: An AI/ML engineer is building a Docker image for a training pipeline that uses PyTorch with CUDA. Which of the following practices will improve build performance, image size, and runtime reproducibility?

options.text: Use a multi-stage build to separate the build-time dependencies (compilers, CUDA toolkit) from the runtime environment
Pin the base image to a specific digest (e.g., nvidia/cuda:12.1.0-base-ubuntu22.04@sha256:...) rather than a mutable tag
Install Python packages with `pip install --no-cache-dir` and clean apt cache in the same RUN layer
Set the working directory to /root to ensure consistent paths across containers
Copy the entire project context with `COPY . .` before installing dependencies to leverage layer caching

question.explanation: Multi-stage builds (a) keep the final image small by discarding build-time tooling. Pinning to a digest (b) guarantees the exact same base image is pulled every time, preventing silent breakages from tag mutations. Combining `--no-cache-dir` with apt cleanup in one RUN layer (c) reduces layer size and avoids caching stale package indexes. Option (d) is not a best practice—/root is not a standard working directory and can cause permission issues; /app or /workspace is preferred. Option (e) is incorrect because copying the entire context before installing dependencies invalidates the cache on any file change; dependencies should be copied and installed first (e.g., COPY requirements.txt . then RUN pip install) to maximize layer reuse.
concepts_tested: Dockerfile best practices for ML workloads
